label: risk-review-1
tail:
All four gates green. Here's what happened.

## The dispatch

The three commands the dispatch names passed on first run — `boundary-audit` and `citation-fidelity` printed no candidates, and `gate-liveness` showed finite-smoke **live at 4 checks**, not vacuous. The real work was the fourth line: `risk-report --require-reviewed` at **125 errors**.

**33 of those 125 weren't missing work.** Alpha-a had written substantive per-item reviews under the key `disposition`; the gate reads `notes`. I read all 33 before touching them — several record confirmed-fatal repairs — and renamed the key. The other **92 were genuinely unreviewed**, and I read and reviewed each one.

## What the reviews turned up

I found a defect class the existing detectors structurally could not see: **17 proof steps that name a check and perform none** — *"We treat the trivial p-subgroup and primes not dividing |G|."*, *"We check the trivial quotient."* Two items (`prop-endomorphisms-form-a-ring`, `thm-endomorphism-ring-of-a-finite-direct-sum-as-hom-matrices`) had **no proof at all** — every numbered step was an announcement. I wrote both proofs.

This is a contract defect, not just prose: `thm-sylow-second-theorem`'s boundary rows were marked `checked` citing step 4.1 — and 4.1 was the announcement. `boundary-audit` only tested that the step *number* existed.

The DeepSeek refuters (Sol is quota-locked — I verified with a live dispatch rather than inheriting the claim) found **zero confirmed fatal defects** across 52 items covered, plus one real miss I fixed: **Sylow III chose a Sylow subgroup with nothing in `deps` establishing one exists**, hidden because step 1.1 blanket-cited all five facts.

## One correction I owe you

Mid-run I told you the Sylow II title defect was fatal. It isn't. Once I self-tested my scan, six other titles used the same convention and `def-sylow-p-subgroup` is defined only for finite groups — so it was underspecified, not false in-library. Recorded as **nonfatal**; I kept the improved title as step-6 polish. That scan first returned zero hits and the zero was meaningless — its regex matched the very title it was meant to flag.

## Left open, deliberately

**518 boundary rows across 88 batch-2 items are generated from a template** that interpolates each item's own title and statement — so no two rows are textually identical and the cluster detector reports nothing across all 518. Batches 1 and 3–7 have none of this. I did not bulk-rewrite them: that's the owning Beta's work with its sources, and a rewrite by me would reproduce the defect in a new hand. Ledgered as `disposition: open`.

**Independent refuter evidence covers 52 of 92 items.** The rest hit the tool-less lane's output budget. I read all 92 myself; the `risk_review` notes say which had corroboration.

I also declined a change that would have looked like an improvement: stripping the title from `boundary-audit`'s cluster key *does* collapse those 518 rows, but it also collapses 45 honest "this item states no biconditional" rows, and that tool's design is precision-first.

Tools added (`announcement-steps.mjs`, `pack-refuter-task.mjs`, `apply-risk-reviews.mjs`) plus the new `boundary-audit` signal are documented in `ARCHITECTURE.md` §3.11g and `QUALITY-CONTROLS.md` in the same change. Five ledger rows appended; 73 rows validate clean. Nothing was committed.
